query: Pockets and Decks Corvin is teaching you to keep your hand in. "Decks are practice," he says, shuffling. "Pockets are performance." Bram is asleep in an armchair nearby, his whistle on a ribbon round his neck. Practise on the deck Two hours of coins and cards until your fingers cramp. It's dull, and by the end the coin vanishes so cleanly even Corvin blinks. "Saint," he says, "with very quick hands." Lift Bram's whistle and return it The whistle comes off its ribbon without a sound and goes back on it the same way. Bram snores through all of it. Corvin is delighted and slightly worried about you.
